rationale: A wins because it knows what will survive a reporter's second question. The line "Do not pitch this without the market list — it is the entire story" is exactly the kind of discipline founders need before they start emailing people. B has usable bones, especially "Wise's stablecoin settlement is a direct shot at correspondent banking's toll booth," but it keeps trying to turn one launch into a market thesis before earning the right.
gaps_in_A: "The businesses waiting three days for a payment that clears in minutes" invents the before-and-after timing. The update says faster and cheaper; it does not give three days, minutes, or a corridor benchmark.
"what changes when settlement is same-day" is another unsupported time claim. Useful shape, bad proof hygiene.
"putting stablecoins on its balance-sheet flows" risks implying Wise balance-sheet exposure before the release says which entity holds the stablecoin or how custody works.
"Not for crypto/token press" is too broad. Crypto-price press is wrong; payments-infrastructure crypto reporters could plausibly care if the stablecoin and partner are real.
gaps_in_B: "category-creation" overclaims. The update gives one Wise launch, not a created category, and B admits it needs "evidence of other regulated payments/financial companies" to make the angle stand up.
"One of the biggest cross-border payment networks" is not stated. £30B per quarter proves scale, not ranking.
"building stablecoin settlement into a core product" goes beyond the facts. The update says Wise is launching the feature for cross-border business payments, not that it is core to the product line.

"cutting correspondent-banking fees is a margin story" assumes Wise's own unit economics improve. The supplied facts only support faster and cheaper movement for businesses unless Wise provides cost or margin disclosure.
The next step, "journalist-fit-check," is premature. Before naming reporters, this needs the stablecoin, partner, launch markets, eligible volume, and comparable cost/time proof.
